summary: Cross-border reporting accountability specificity pass: international coordination, customs/CBAM, remittance corridors, immigration/asylum/status fees, withholding/treaty/MAP relief, and GIR/claim-split routes now name concrete actors, beneficiaries, bottlenecks, evidence, fallback dispute paths, and capacity duties.
north_star: Route fiscal design by control, benefit, burden, capacity, protected floors, public legitimacy, territory/commons constraints, strategic capacity, private gatekeeping, care finance, classification seams, private rails, source currentness, executable regression cases, and policy-action semantics.
core_claims: Cross-border routes must separate coordination bodies, customs and CBAM registries, remittance rails, status-fee gates, withholding/reclaim/MAP channels, GIR exchange, claim-split formulas, protected burden bearers, and source-state capacity duties; foreignness, visible remitter status, or claimant status does not assign responsibility by itself.
Actor accountability must separate controller, beneficiary, remitter, bottleneck channel, burden bearer, non-responsible conduit, and public fallback-duty owner.
Tax-administration access routes must name the concrete access-rent beneficiary and route-specific evidence before assigning fault, delay, fee, or fallback duty.

Controller-AI routes must name the human, firm, agency, signer, vendor, controller group, or public fallback owner with real control, benefit, bottleneck power, or evidence access; a model score or AI-law title is not itself an accountable actor.

Labor/care routes must separate work controllers, household or care record holders, benefit administrators, credential gates, pension/plan actors, data controllers, burden bearers, and public fallback owners.
The instrument label is not the policy action; each route has a policy-action profile.
A user fee needs a special-benefit or cost/value nexus, review discipline, and essential-access protection.
Tax-like revenue, rent capture, and harm pricing require incidence, authority, representation, and proceeds review.
Non-compensable or cumulative harm should escalate to duty, permit denial, siting veto, or no-go rule rather than price.
Compensation and rebates must reach the real burden bearer through a workable channel, not merely the legal remitter.
A remedy_type axis value is not yet a remedy; each route needs a default move, blocked move, guardrails, escalation trigger, and proceeds-integrity posture.
Golden cases are executable answer contracts with expected routes, valid axes, flags, remedy obligations, sources, and must-not answers.
Source-currentness refs are release-critical dependencies, not ordinary citations; each needs a local claim and review reason.
Every calibration ladder must be indexed in cube-index.json or explicitly exempted.
scorecard-template.json is canonical; proposal-scorecard.md must be rendered from it.
Mandatory private rails require public/no-rent fallback, fee controls, portability, and no forfeiture from rail failure.
Taxpayer-side AI and preparer tools require accountable signatures, source traceability, taxpayer review, refund control, and victim relief.
Release integrity requires manifest hashes, handoff text, receipt metadata, and package naming to agree with the active revision.
